text: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we think about creativity. Today, AI can generate paintings, compose music, and even write stories and poems. While these outputs can be impressive and sometimes beautiful, there is a fundamental difference between human and machine creativity. Machines, like LLMs or generative AI, learn from vast amounts of existing data. They combine and rearrange patterns they have seen, but they do not have personal experiences, emotions, or intentions. Human creativity, in contrast, often springs from a unique perspective, a feeling, or a desire to communicate. It involves making choices that are meaningful to us. While AI can be a powerful tool to assist artists and writers, it is unlikely to ever replace the deep, personal spark that makes human art truly original.
